candidate.answerReason: Multiplying both dimensions by 1.1 multiplies their perimeter by 1.1, an increase of 10%.

methods.label: Scale the perimeter
methods.explanation:
Perimeter adds side lengths, so the common increase factor can be factored out of the sum. Let the original length and width be \(\ell>0\) and \(w>0\). The original perimeter is \(P=2(\ell+w)>0\).

A \(10\%\) increase multiplies each dimension by \(1.1\), so the new perimeter is
\[
2(1.1\ell+1.1w)=1.1\,[2(\ell+w)]=1.1P.
\]
The increase is therefore \(0.1P\), which is \(\boxed{10\%}\) of the original perimeter, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the rectangle perimeter formula, percent factors, and one elementary distributive step.
